title: Customer Signal Funnel for Prioritized Roadmap Input
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood receives a high volume of signals from enterprise accounts (CSM requests, escalations, support tickets, renewal risk conversations, and high-value POCs). Currently these signals are inconsistently captured and routed to product, which causes ad-hoc roadmap changes, missed SLAs, and reactive prioritization.

Goal:
Create a repeatable customer signal funnel and scoring model that converts top-account inputs into prioritized roadmap candidates with clear SLAs, owners, and transparency to GTM and engineering. The funnel should scale across hosted, dedicated, and private customers and feed into quarterly planning and OKR tracking.

Success metrics (initial):
- Time from signal capture to prioritization decision <= 10 business days for top-tier accounts
- 80% of prioritized items have a documented owner, impact statement, and rough estimate
- Reduction in duplicate requests surfaced to PM/Eng by 40% via centralized signal deduplication
- Measurable correlation between prioritized items and renewal/conversion outcomes (preliminary analysis on 20 accounts)

Scope (in):
- Define signal taxonomy (ticket, CSM escalation, sales ask, NPS comment, telemetry spike)
- Build triage workflows and SLA tiers (T1: urgent top-account escalations, T2: strategic feature asks, T3: general backlog)
- Prioritization rubric combining revenue exposure, recurrence, technical effort, strategic alignment, and risk
- Intake form/template for CSMs and Support with autopopulating account metadata
- Dashboards for PM/Revenue/GTM to track funnel movement and decisions

Scope (out):
- Full automation of engineering estimations (we will use rough sizing from Eng leads initially)
- Rewriting support ticketing system — we will integrate with existing tools instead

Proposed funnel (high-level):
1) Capture: standardized intake form + automatic ingestion from priority support queues and renewal notes.
2) Enrich: attach account metadata (ARR, tier, active POCs), recent SLO incidents, and relevant PRs or incident reports.
3) Score: apply prioritization rubric to produce a raw score and tier (A/B/C).
4) Triage meeting: weekly triage where PM lead makes provisional decision for A/B items; C items batched into backlog grooming.
5) Decision & Routing: approved A items get assigned to a project or spike with a target kickoff window; B items get grooming and potential inclusion in next cycle.
6) Feedback loop: customers receive status within SLA windows and GTM/CSM playbooks updated.

Prioritization rubric (prototype):
- Revenue exposure (0-40): ARR at risk, potential upsell, contract size
- Recurrence (0-20): number of distinct customers requesting or telemetry frequency
- Strategic alignment (0-20): maps to Q2 strategic initiatives/OKRs
- Technical effort (0-15): rough estimate from Eng lead (lower score for higher effort)
- Operational risk / Compliance (0-5): regulatory or security urgency
Final score normalized to 100; threshold for "A" >= 65.

Acceptance criteria:
- PM intake template available in Confluence and linked from CSM playbook
- Automated ingestion from two priority support queues and one CSM email alias
- Triage workflow documented with owners and SLAs (T1: 24h response, T2: 3 business days, T3: 10 business days)
- Dashboard in Console showing funnel counts, average time-in-stage, and top scored items
- Pilot executed with three enterprise customers over 6 weeks and learnings documented

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-2: finalize signal taxonomy and intake template (PM + Design + CSM)
- Week 3-4: implement ingestion and enrichment (ENG support: integrations with Zendesk and internal CSM tracker)
- Week 5: run scoring engine (initial spreadsheet prototype -> small internal service)
- Week 6-9: pilot with 3 customers, gather feedback, iterate rubric
- Week 10: present results to Product Council and recommend Q2 roadmap injections

Open questions / risks:
- Will Engineering commit rough effort estimates for triage? (Mitigation: time-boxed spike to get ballpark estimates)
- Data privacy for enrichment when pulling customer telemetry into a centralized system (Mitigation: only ingest metadata and Links to anonymized dashboards; engage Security)
- Change management for CSMs — risk of low adoption (Mitigation: slot time for two enablement sessions and embed into renewal cadence)

Stakeholders:
- PM lead: Aisha Patel
- Eng leads: Marcus Liu (runtime), Irene Gomez (integrations)
- Head of CS: Laura Chen
- Sales ops: Rajiv Menon

Deliverables:
- Confluence PRD and intake template
- Ingestion integration (Zendesk -> triage queue) and enrichment job
- Prioritization scoring spreadsheet and calculation service
- Triage runbook and SLA matrix
- Pilot report and decision memo for Product Council

Notes:
This ticket aims to reduce ad-hoc priority changes driven by individual AE/CSM pressure and create a transparent, measurable path from customer signal to roadmap action. We will keep the rubric visible and editable by a small cross-functional committee to tune weights based on pilot outcomes.
